review_locator: PMCID:PMC2794881, DAP10- and DAP12-associated receptors in innate immunity
primary_title: The activating NKG2D receptor assembles in the membrane with two signaling dimers into a hexameric structure; NKG2D recruits two distinct adapters to trigger NK cell activation and costimulation
decision_basis: Primary structural/biochemical and adapter-deficiency studies support exact NKG2D-DAP10 membrane assembly and adapter-dependent receptor expression/function
limitations_preserved: Preserve two-DAP10-dimer stoichiometry, human/mouse adapter branch differences and no SCI/terminal-TF inference.

primary_title: DAP10 associates with Ly49 receptors but contributes minimally to their expression and function in vivo
decision_basis: Primary NK-cell immunoprecipitation and deficiency comparisons support Ly49D-DAP10 association, with a small surface-expression contribution and DAP12-dominant context
limitations_preserved: Preserve minor DAP10 association and dominant DAP12 usage; no DAP10-dependent Ly49D effector-function claim.

primary_title: DAP10 associates with Ly49 receptors but contributes minimally to their expression and function in vivo; Ly49H signaling through DAP10 is essential for optimal natural killer cell responses to mouse cytomegalovirus infection
decision_basis: Primary NK-cell association/deficiency studies and MCMV-response perturbation support Ly49H-DAP10 association with a bounded additional antiviral contribution alongside DAP12
